answer: A CONTEXT.md file must be **"under 80 lines"** (_core/CONVENTIONS.md, Quality Guardrails), and Pattern 6 says this keeps them **"small (25-80 lines)"**. The Stage 03 audit wording differs slightly: it passes if **"No CONTEXT.md file exceeds 80 lines"**, which would allow exactly 80, while Stage 05 flags any file **"over 80 lines"**.
Reference files should stay "under 200 lines"; if a file runs longer, "split into multiple files" (per _core/CONVENTIONS.md).
Placeholder names use "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" inside double braces, for example `{{BRAND_NAME}}`, written as `{{SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE}}`.

Onboarding is complete "only when zero placeholders remain," meaning there are no remaining `{{` patterns anywhere in the workspace after replacement. If any remain, the agent flags them and asks the user for the missing information.

The `status` trigger scans `stages/*/output/`, and a stage is COMPLETE if its output folder "contains files (other than .gitkeep)." If the folder "is empty or contains only .gitkeep," the stage is PENDING.
It goes in the `references/` folder of the stage that uses it (e.g., `stages/03-build/references/remotion-setup.md`). A tool needed by multiple stages can live in `shared/` instead.

If any audit check fails, "the agent revises before saving to output/" (_core/CONVENTIONS.md, Pattern 12); the stage files say the same, e.g. "If any fail, revise before saving," and the scaffolding stage says "If any fail, fix before saving."
Under Pattern 3 in _core/CONVENTIONS.md, every folder points outward to what it needs and no folder points back, because this "prevents reference growth from going N-squared as the system scales."
Layer 0, `CLAUDE.md`, is "always loaded," at about "~800 tokens."
You write "Full file" in the Section/Scope column (per Pattern 4: Selective Section Routing in `_core/CONVENTIONS.md`).
The pinned JEV model is **jev-1.14.0**. `shared/constants.md` says it is "Pinned so cutoffs stay valid", and the questionnaire default calls it "pinned; cutoffs re-checked on it".
HCES timings must use a monotonic clock (`time.perf_counter_ns`), never wall-clock time.

A needle is one of the "Short invented passages, written in the volume's style, inserted between real passages," and "Each needle is the only place its question is answered." About 10 are planted per volume, spread "across the start, middle and end of each volume."
The memory stream data is about Quillmere Broadband, described as "a made-up regional home-internet provider" whose facts keep changing ("plan prices, outage fixes, refund rules").
The memory stream is "About 300 dated records, about 200k tokens."
No. HCES does not inherit "Any HTES cutoff value"; instead, "Cutoffs are set fresh in stage 04."
The HCES gate returns "not in the documents" instead of padding the context when the evidence is not enough (Pattern 16 in `_core/CONVENTIONS.md`).

Selected skills are copied (local) or cloned (GitHub) into the workspace's `skills/` folder **"during scaffolding (Stage 03)"**. Local skills found in `~/.claude/skills/` or `~/.agents/skills/` have their entire folder copied into `skills/[skill-name]/`.
JEV costs **$0.042 per million input tokens, output free** (constants.md lists this value for cost estimates).

After every run, update `stages/01-setup-smoke/output/core-design.md` and `core-design.html` "with the real results, rubrics in use, metrics, and any design change the run forced." Every run must also log access, analysis and response time in `shared/timings.md`.
In the script-to-animation example, agents leave the **"Strategic Rationale"** section unloaded; they "load the rules sections, not the strategic rationale."
The hard cases are "Low overlap: the answer shares few words with the question" and "Lookalikes: passages that use the question's words but do not answer it."

Em dashes are banned throughout: the conventions say "No em dashes anywhere in the repo" and HCES Lab says "No em dashes in any file," with the Stage 01 audit checking for "None in new files." During validation, any em dashes found are to be replaced with "--".

Per `_core/CONVENTIONS.md` (Pattern 11), "Checkpoints go between process steps, not within them." The agent finishes a full unit of work, presents options or a draft, and the human redirects before the next unit begins.
